about: How a theme resolves (DESIGN section 1.5, T1): what it sets, for light or dark mode. A color is "#rrggbb" as written, or "@role" for a role the theme does not set, which keeps the value of Clarity's own theme. Parts are keyed by kind, or kind:state. clarity_spec::themes::resolve gives these, and each stack is written from it: the web renderer as a CSS file per theme (clarity_gen::theme_css), Avalonia as resources. mode and dark say whether the theme shows dark for the system's choice, which the web renderer checks too.

resolves.what: light mode with a color of its own, a font, a size, a radius and styles

theme.source:
theme Case
    mode system
    color accent "#2f6fdf" dark "#5b8cff"
    color brand "#f5c400"
    font "Inter"
    size 14
    radius 6
    style primary background accent, text "#fff"
    style loud background brand, text text, border none

resolves.what: dark mode, with a part in a state, roles, spacing, a shadow and a bold style

theme.source:
theme Case
    mode system
    color accent "#2f6fdf" dark "#5b8cff"
    color brand "#f5c400"
    size small 11
    radius input 3
    padding 6
    border 2
    shadow flat
    part button hover background accent_soft, radius 4
    style primary background accent, border brand, weight bold

resolves.what: a light theme stays light on a dark system

theme.source:
theme Case
    mode light
    color background "#ffffff" dark "#000000"
